question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{-(x+y)}, & x\ge 0,\,y\ge 0, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

The marginal CDF ${F}_{X}(x)$ of $X$ is given by

$$
{F}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0 \\ g(x), & x\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

What is the function $g(x)?$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $X$ for $x\ge 0$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-(x+y)}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={e}^{-x}{lim}_{b\to \infty }{\int }_{0}^{b}{e}^{-y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={e}^{-x}{lim}_{b\to \infty }{[-{e}^{-y}]}_{y=0}^{y=b} \\  & ={e}^{-x}{lim}_{b\to \infty }(1-{e}^{-b}) \\  & ={e}^{-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the marginal CDF of $X$ for $x\ge 0$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}{f}_{X}(u)\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{x}{e}^{-u}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={[-{e}^{-u}]}_{0}^{x} \\  & =1-{e}^{-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${F}_{X}(x)$ is

$$
{F}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0 \\ 1-{e}^{-x}, & x\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $g(x)=1-{e}^{-x}.$
